text:
deploy-bot: Rollout paused: canary 2/3 in euw2-a10-l4 showing p99 latency spike (+45%) vs baseline. Auto-rollback disabled for this rollout.

maria: I'm seeing a KV cache miss surge correlated with the spike. Miss rate jumped from 2% -> 18% at 09:12.

liam: Network counters on the affected hosts show increased retransmits on eth0. suspect NIC saturation / queueing.

sam: CI perf job a10-l4-nightly also failed this morning: p99 +30% after merge 4128 (kernel-picker heuristics). @liam can you bisect?

liam: Starting bisect range: before 4110 -> after 4135. Quick check: the only large change touching kernel selection + batching was 4128.

jen: Adding data: flamegraph from 09:10 (canary) vs baseline. Attaching gist: https://internal.gist/fg/euw2-a10-canary-0910 (perm:eng). Key diff: more time in io_wait + net_rx_softirq.

maria: Sample KV cache log snippet:
```
[09:11:58] kvcache: miss (key=chat/context/xx) -> backend fetch 14ms
[09:12:03] kvcache: miss (prefix hit rate dropped)\n```
Seems like cache pressure + network stalls causing backend fetch latency to balloon.

ryan: On the same hosts, ethtool -S shows high rx_packets and rx_dropped counters. Also saw ECMP flow skewing on switch side. Might be an asymmetric path causing reordering and retries.

sam: Could be noisy neighbor VM in same host hogging NIC. Any pcap or tc metrics?

liam: I ran tcpdump for 30s during peak, saw retransmit bursts and out-of-order segments. Also eBPF trace shows increased sys_read on network sockets.

jen: Reminder: 4128 changed kernel selection to prefer L4-optimized kernels for small batches which increases concurrent NIC usage (more frequent small transmissions). On A10 NICs this could amplify interrupts.

maria: Hypothesis: change in kernel selection increased the pattern of small packet bursts, exposing a NIC driver scheduling pathology on A10 hosts in euw2 under certain ECMP distributions. H100 cluster not affected because different NICs and batch distribution.

liam: Quick repro: run internal loadgen with --batch-strategy=small-bursts and target a10-l4 pool. Command:
```
$ /ops/loadgen --target=euw2-a10-l4 --model=gpt-small --batch-strategy=small-bursts --concurrency=120 --duration=60s
```
Reproduction locally gave +40% p99 within 30s.

sam: Options: revert 4128, or patch kernel picker to fall back to previous batching distribution for pools with NIC telemetry indicating rx_drop>0.1% (temporary guard).

jen: CI shows that reverting 4128 removes regression on a10-l4-nightly. I pushed a revert PR 4143.

ci-bot: CI results for revert PR 4143: a10-l4-nightly p99 back to baseline (+2% noise), all tests passing.

liam: Rolling revert to euw2 canary now, will hold and watch.

deploy-bot: Revert 4143 deployed to euw2 canary at 09:25.

maria: After revert, KV cache miss rate back to 3%, rx_dropped counters returning to baseline on canary hosts.

ryan: Confirmed: tcpdump no longer shows retransmit bursts, E2E latency stabilized.

sam: Filing follow-ups: 1) proper kernel-picker patch that accounts for NIC telemetry + ECMP skewing, 2) add perf CI job that runs small-burst microbenchmark on A10 NICs, 3) telemetry alert when rx_drop spikes >0.05% during rollouts.

liam: Created issues: INF-1287 (picker fix), INF-1288 (a10 microbenchmark), INF-1289 (telemetry alert).

jen: Thanks everyone. Leaving rollout paused until we validate revert across all EUW2 A10 nodes. Ping me in thread when metrics are green for 30m. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout remains paused. Monitoring window started 09:26. Next update expected around 09:56.
